pages.text: "Wow, raspberries!" Mom had said he could pick from this bush. Pipo plucked berries, soon heaping his basket. "I will eat all of these!" He swallowed eagerly.
Long-necked Mrs. Goose climbed the hill with her goslings. "Pipo, let us see your raspberries too!" He hugged the basket and turned away. "No, all mine!"
Sadly, Mrs. Goose and the goslings went downhill. Alone, Pipo ate one berry, then another. Somehow it was no fun. "Oh? Why am I not happy at all?"
Mom came and sat beside him. "Pipo, your basket is full. Why is your face so sad?" He tilted his head. "Lots of berries... why is it not fun?"
Smiling, Mom split one raspberry in half. "Sharing tasty things in halves makes them tastier. Half each tastes even better!" His eyes sparkled. "Really? Half each?"
Pipo carried his basket downhill. "Mrs. Goose, I am sorry! Let us eat together!" She stretched her neck, eyes wide. Goslings peeped too.
"One, ask first! Two, divide into halves!" With both hands, Pipo pushed berries into two halves. One for Mrs. Goose's family, one for him—equally heaped. "Half each tastes even better!"
"Three, sit side by side and eat!" Goslings pecked, Pipo munched. Mrs. Goose stretched her neck and repeated, "Half each tastes even better!" Pipo crouched on the grass with hands at his chest.
At dinner, Pipo split bread in half first. "Mom, eat with me! One, ask first! Two, divide into halves! Three, sit side by side and eat!" He made the same gestures as on the hill.
Pipo hugged Mom's neck and offered half the bread into her mouth. "Your share!" Sharing tasty halves doubled smiles too. Into her ear, he called, "Half each tastes even better!"
